title: Starts with a, or ends in b: why the dead state matters
notes: A has no move from p0 on b, so Build first gives A a dead state. Read b first and A falls into it, but B keeps going: (dead, q1) accepts, because the word ends in b. Leave the dead state out and the union loses every word that starts and ends with b.
ops: start p0; accept p1; p0 a -> p1; p1 a,b -> p1 | start q0; accept q1; q0 a -> q0; q0 b -> q1; q1 a -> q0; q1 b -> q1
